articles.title: Lady Frost eyes Major League Wrestling women's title, touts 'incredible roster'
articles.summary: Lady Frost declared herself the top contender for Shotzi's MLW Women's World Championship and says she'll do whatever it takes to claim the gold.
articles.body: Lady Frost has her eyes on the Major League Wrestling (MLW) Women’s World Championship and is willing to do whatever it takes get some gold wrapped around her waist. Shotzi found herself a challenger in Lady Frost over the last few weeks after she rose in MLW to grab the title from Shoko Nakajima on MLW "Fusion" back in June. Frost came out to confront Shotzi on last week’s episode, appearing to declare herself the top contender for the belt. COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK "Well, if you've seen anything that I've done lately – because you did say you've been watching — I am a fighter. I have everything to prove and that's the No. 1 spot and I deserve it. That's it. It's as simple as that," Lady Frost told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview. Frost said she would give "everything" to get that championship. "Literally everything. That's the goal," she said. "And I'm willing to do whatever it takes to get it." Frost was one of MLW’s marquee signings this year to bolster its women’s division. She shared some light on why she decided to sign with MLW back in April. "So, the conversation that we had was very valuable to me because they've been watching me for a very long time, not just my work in the past few years," she said. "And I think it's important for someone to believe in you creatively and as a performer in general. And I think they have all the confidence in the world in me. And that's exactly what I wanted to hear. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS "I felt like it was a good fit because all of the women there are trying to prove something because they're either brand new, trying to make a name for themselves, trying to rebuild, or just make this women's division even tougher than it already is." MLW also has alliances with Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) and Stardom, which allows for the roster to mix it up with opponents from around the world. Frost said those relationships were a part of the intrigue. "I think I've done numerous tours in CMLL and that's a great fit for me. And then the girls of Stardom, obviously those are great matches," she said. "I love working those girls. And then there's the independents, which I feel like was very healthy for me to get back into creatively. "It's not all about hitting your times and being on camera and doing things appropriately. It's reminding ourselves why we do this and what we're fighting for, and most times it's the fans, right? So, having a little bit of everything right now while focusing on that title for MLW has really been great for my career." Frost is set to take on Corinne Joy at MLW’s Kings of Colosseum event. The top stars on the roster will be on display, including Killer Kross, Josh Bishop, Diego Hill, Templario and others. The event will be free on YouTube, beIN Sports and Veeps. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We have an incredible roster. We have great production. I think it's unique in its own way and it's not something that some people might feel overproduced in a way that feels artificial," Frost added. "I think it feels very raw and real. And you see so many different unique styles. And yes, we partner with CMLL, so you will see that lucha style. You're going to see that grittiness. You're going to see darkness. There's something for everyone."

articles.title: Major disruption as grass fire hits Heathrow train links
articles.summary: Severe delays and cancellations are set to continue, with no trains between central London and the airport.
articles.body:
Trains to and from Heathrow Airport have been halted after a trackside grass fire caused delays and cancellations.

National Rail said "major disruption" was expected until the end of Saturday following the incident which began shortly after 16:00 BST.

A statement said all lines were blocked between London Paddington station and Heathrow's terminals, as well as Reading, due to "a failure of the electricity supply caused by a fire next to the track".

An update from Network Rail Western late on Saturday said the fire had been extinguished, but warned that disruption would continue, possibly into Sunday morning for some services.

It comes hours after a separate grass fire on Heathrow's airfield shut a runway earlier on Saturday.

Pictures on social media showed crowds of stranded passengers at Paddington, one of London's main rail hubs.

London Fire Brigade said six fire engines and around 40 crew members were tackling the blaze near Scrubs Lane, North Kensington.

Great Western Railway cancelled its services to Reading and no Elizabeth line or Heathrow Express services were running between Paddington and Heathrow on Saturday night.

The airport advised passengers to leave extra time for their journeys, adding that the Piccadilly line, which runs services to the airport, also has delays.

Network Rail Western said some services on Sunday morning could face delays and cancellations, caused by trains being displaced by the disruption.

Earlier on Saturday, Heathrow's southern runway was closed while crews tackled a grass fire on the airfield.

It caused some disruption with at least two flights diverted elsewhere. Heathrow apologised for any disruption and said the fire was extinguished quickly.

That comes weeks after another grass fire near Heathrow's southern runway which forced 18 flights to divert and destroyed a large area of grassland.

While weather has cooled across much of the UK in recent days following record-breaking heat over the summer, fire crews have still been warning of wildfire risks.

The Met Office's Fire Severity Index shows that if a wildfire was to occur, it would have a "high" fire severity in most of south-east England and some of the Midlands.

The fire severity is "exceptional", the highest level on the index, in some parts of London including Heathrow, as well as on the Essex and Suffolk coasts.

articles.title: Minecraft Wilderness Bound update: Release date, features, and more details
articles.summary: Esports News: The Minecraft 26.3 update has officially received its name: the Wilderness Bound update. Confirmed as the next Main Drop releasing this month, Wildern.
articles.body: The Minecraft 26.3 update has officially received its name: the Wilderness Bound update. Confirmed as the next Main Drop releasing this month, Wilderness Bound is shaping up to be one of the most charming and exploration-focused drops of the year.This is going to be pretty different from the underground-focused Chaos Cubed drop, and you can expect it to bring a variety of things, including a brand-new biome, a new wood type, camping-focused furniture blocks, and a new structure to discover out in the wild.In the section below, we provide you with everything we know about the Minecraft Wilderness Bound update, including its release date, features, and more.Minecraft Wilderness Bound update release dateMojang has not confirmed a concrete release date for the Minecraft 26.3 drop, but it is expected to arrive in the period of the next two weeks. This means that Wilderness Bound is likely to release around mid-September.Essentially, it will release as Java Edition 26.3 and Bedrock Edition 26.50. There are a lot of features arriving as part of the same, including the Dappled Forest biome, new blocks, and more.Minecraft Wilderness Bound update featuresThe Dappled Forest biomeDappled Forest is the new biome arriving with the Minecraft Wilderness Bound update, and it is filled with red, orange and yellow Poplar trees. Poplar saplings grow into any one of red, orange, or yellow poplar trees and can be sold by a wandering trader.Unstripped poplar logs can also be sold by wandering traders. The biome also features red shrubs, which are bush-like plant blocks found in small patches.New building blocksThe update adds wool stairs and slabs, concrete stairs and slabs, straw beds, and cushions to the game. Concrete stairs and concrete slabs round out the update across all sixteen dye colors.You can turn hardened concrete blocks into stairs and slabs just like stone, getting the flat architectural gradients that were previously impossible with plain full blocks. It is a long-overdue addition that the building community has been requesting for years.Straw Beds and CushionsStraw Beds are arriving with the new Minecraft update and they allow you to skip a night without changing the respawn point. You can find these beds at the Abandoned Camps or use 3x Hay Bales to craft one.Speaking of Cushions, they are a new decorative seat block that pair naturally with Straw Beds to give interiors a soft, homey layer that Minecraft's blocky palette has always struggled to deliver.Abandoned CampsA new structure called the abandoned camp is being added as part of the Wilderness Bound update. Scattered throughout the Dappled Forest, abandoned camps are small tent-like structures built from wool stairs and featuring chests or barrels to loot.This was all you needed to know about the Minecraft Wilderness Bound update.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 49ers dealt major blow before season opener as star player lands on injured reserve
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers have made a significant roster move involving veteran defensive end Sam Okuayinonu after his foot injury ruled him out of their season op...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers have made a significant roster move involving veteran defensive end Sam Okuayinonu after his foot injury ruled him out of their season opener.

Okuayinonu has been placed on injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least the first four games of the 2026 season.

The defensive end did not travel to Australia with the rest of the 49ers after suffering the foot injury, and he was subsequently ruled out of San Francisco's Week 1 clash with the Los Angeles Rams.

Sam Okuayinonu placed on injured reserve

The latest move represents a further setback for Okuayinonu after the injury prevented him from joining the team in Australia.

"49ers sign Jon Weeks to 53 along with Khalid Kareem from practice squad, place Sam Okuayinonu on IR," Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston shared in a post on X.

Okuayinonu had played an unexpectedly important role for the 49ers in 2025. After featuring in a reserve role in 2024, he started 12 of the 15 games he played last season, recording 39 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble.

His role was expected to decrease in 2026, but he was still projected to remain an important part of San Francisco's defensive line.

The foot injury has now disrupted those plans, with Okuayinonu set to miss at least the opening four games after being placed on injured reserve.

The 49ers also made additional roster moves alongside Okuayinonu's placement on IR, signing Jon Weeks to the 53-man roster and promoting Khalid Kareem from the practice squad.

Okuayinonu's absence now leaves San Francisco without the veteran defensive end for the opening stretch of the regular season as the team prepares to begin its campaign against the Rams.

articles.title: Why Nuggets Fans Should Believe Jokić’s ‘Okay’ Prediction
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić does not do empty optimism. So when the three-time MVP was asked about the Denver Nuggets’ decision to trade Peyton Watson and offered a calm as...
articles.body:
Nikola Jokić does not do empty optimism. So when the three-time MVP was asked about the Denver Nuggets' decision to trade Peyton Watson and offered a calm assessment of the team's future, it carried more weight than the usual offseason platitudes.

After leading Serbia past Victor Wembanyama and France in a FIBA World Cup qualifier, Jokić addressed the multi-team sign-and-trade that sent Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

"I'm happy for Peyton," he said . "He deserved it. We will miss his energy and skill. I don't think about the season yet; we have to play this, but it's gonna be okay."

The quote, delivered while Jokić focused on national-team duties, quickly circulated among Nuggets fans still processing a first-round playoff exit and a quiet, financially constrained offseason. The natural question followed: Should they take him at his word?

Watson's Departure Left a Hole Denver Couldn't Fully Fill

Watson emerged as a key two-way piece in 2025-26. In 54 games (40 starts), the 6-foot-8 wing averaged 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 0.9 steals and 1.1 blocks while shooting 49.1 percent from the field and 41.1 percent from three. His athleticism and defensive versatility filled a clear need alongside Jokić and Jamal Murray .

Denver ultimately signed-and-traded the restricted free agent to Cleveland as part of a multi-team deal. The Nuggets received an unprotected 2031 first-round pick from the Cavaliers and a 2032 second-round selection. No rotation player of note came back the other way. Cap and luxury-tax realities, including second-apron restrictions, heavily influenced the decision.

Days later, Denver signed veteran scorer DeMar DeRozan to a one-year, $3.9 million deal to bolster bench scoring and creation. The move added a proven mid-range specialist and secondary playmaker, but it did not fully replace Watson's two-way profile or youth.

Jokić Has Earned the Right to Be Taken at His Word

After the Nuggets' first-round loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Jokić did not sugarcoat the situation. He acknowledged the team was "far away" from true title contention while still reaffirming his desire to remain a Nugget long-term. That same straightforward style makes his more recent "okay" comment harder to dismiss as pure spin or public-relations damage control.

The 2025-26 season was plagued by injuries. Jokić missed time with a hyperextended left knee. Gordon dealt with hamstring and calf issues. Braun missed large stretches with an ankle sprain, Johnson was limited by a knee bone bruise, and Watson's hamstring injury kept him out of the playoffs entirely. Despite all of that, Denver still finished with 54 wins and the No. 3 seed.

Jokić averaged another near triple-double season, leading the league in both rebounds and assists. When healthy, the Jokić-Murray two-man game remains one of the most difficult actions in basketball to defend, and Gordon continues to provide the two-way versatility and physicality that complements the star center.

"Okay" may simply mean competitive and playoff-relevant rather than championship favorite. An honest reading of a roster operating under tight financial constraints.

The unprotected 2031 first-round pick acquired in the Watson deal gives Denver future asset flexibility that could be used to address depth or athleticism later. Jokić has repeatedly shown an ability to elevate the players around him, turning role players into productive pieces through his vision and decision-making.

His current priority remains practical: finishing national-team duties with Serbia before shifting full attention to training camp and the upcoming season. That grounded mindset has served him and the franchise for years.

Watson represented developing two-way athleticism and defensive versatility in the heart of Jokić's prime years. Losing that production without a comparable replacement thins the wing rotation at a time when the Western Conference is loaded with physical, switchable teams.

DeRozan helps on offense as a mid-range creator and secondary playmaker. However, at 37, he is a fundamentally different type of player—more isolation scorer than the athletic, switchable defender Watson provided.

The broader picture raises sharper questions. Injuries plagued the 2025-2026 season and repeatedly disrupted continuity. Multiple starters missed significant stretches, forcing the team to lean on younger or less proven pieces for long periods. Those absences contributed to an uneven regular season and left the roster less prepared for playoff physicality.

The No. 6-seeded Timberwolves eliminated the Nuggets 4-2 in the first round. This was even after Minnesota lost Anthony Edwards and other key contributors during the series. It marked the first time since 2022 that Denver failed to advance past the first round, exposing lingering issues with rebounding, defensive consistency, and supporting scoring.

The Cap, the Coach, and an Aging Core Add Uncertainty

Head coach David Adelman's situation adds another layer of uncertainty.

Denver fired Michael Malone late in the 2024-25 season, and Adelman stepped in as interim and guided the team to the second round. He earned the full-time job, but his first full season as head coach ended in that early exit.

While the front office has publicly backed him, the jump from successful assistant/interim to sustained head-coaching success is never guaranteed. The first-round loss invited scrutiny about scheme, adjustments, and in-game management against a physical opponent.

Looking ahead, the salary-cap picture is bleak for an aging core . The Nuggets are already operating deep into second-apron territory with massive contracts for Jokić, Murray, Gordon, Braun, and others. Denver projects enormous luxury-tax bills, and apron restrictions severely limit the ability to add meaningful talent via free agency or trade.

Jokić is 31; Murray and Gordon are also in or approaching their 30s. Without significant roster upgrades, the championship window could narrow.

Denver risks a stretch of competitive-but-not-elite seasons. Fans watched Watson break out, then watched him leave. Now they're asking: are low-cost moves like the DeRozan signing enough to keep Denver from settling for 'okay'?

Jokić Is Setting a Floor, Not Making a Promise

Jokić's comment is best read as a floor assessment, not a ceiling prediction.

The Nuggets remain a playoff team with arguably the best player in the world. They are not, on paper, the clear contender many hoped for after the championship core's earlier peaks.

Believing Jokić does not require ignoring the roster holes or financial limits. It means accepting that his honesty usually tracks reality. He is not promising a title run. He is saying the team will be functional and competitive, an understated baseline that matches both his personality and the current construction of the roster.

Whether that is enough for Nuggets fans depends on what they expect from the Jokić era in its later stages. The star has given his measured take. The front office still has work to do to make "okay" feel like more than a consolation.
